q: A 68-metric evaluation framework organized across three orthogonal dimensions
r: Include: new benchmark and evaluation method for AI app builders creating and modifying whole applications from business requirements (project level).

q: Builders see hidden specifications and produce repositories
r: Include: builder-finder protocol is a new evaluation method (recovery, stability, repeated trials) on agents building repositories from specifications.

q: SWE-CHAIN: We introduce the first benchmark for chained release-level maintenance
r: Include: new benchmark where agents implement version-upgrade specifications at feature level, chained across releases; not SWE-bench issue repair.

q: a benchmark of 115 real open-source version-upgrade tasks across 17 repositories
r: Include: new benchmark of multi-target feature development from roadmap specifications across many repositories and languages.

q: evaluates whether coding agents can turn a frozen Structured WebGame Specification into a browser-accessible game
r: Include: new requirement-to-application benchmark and runtime evaluation method comparing 12 coding agents.

q: We propose ProcCtrlBench, a benchmark for execution-process evaluation in LLM coding agents beyond final outcomes
r: EC6: evaluates execution trajectories sampled mostly from SWE-bench-Verified and TerminalBench, not application development from requirements.

q: This leaves out a basic question: can an agent keep its own codebase working as requirements change
r: Include: new multi-round benchmark where agents build and evolve codebases from requirements, with new metrics and repeated attempts.

q: VISTA turns design handoffs into application-construction tasks that require integrated frontend, backend, and database implementations across 18 applications
r: Include: new benchmark for building full-stack applications from designs, with component-level executable evaluation and workflow analysis.

q: the first web generation benchmark that systematically evaluates code agents under underspecified user requests with multi-round interactive refinement
r: Include: new benchmark and feedback-based evaluation protocol for agents building web projects from underspecified requests.

q: We argue that current coding benchmarks are misaligned with agentic software engineering
r: EC3: short position paper (about 7 pages) with no empirical evaluation; an argument about benchmarks.
